edges.mechanism: Product supplies vitamin K1 1500 mcg + MK-4 5 mg + MK-7 600 mcg; vitamin K competitively antagonizes warfarin, lowering INR; MK-7 has a long half-life and accumulates. Astaxanthin raised INR in one case report, adding unpredictability.
edges.evidence: Label: increased vitamin K intake decreases INR response; dose-response study: MK-7 10-45 mcg/d clinically lowered INR; MK-7 >=50 mcg/d flagged as relevant; case report with astaxanthin; moderate certainty for direction

edges.mechanism: Same vitamin K-mediated antagonism of VKA anticoagulation; MK-7 45 mcg/d lowered INR ~40% in acenocoumarol-treated volunteers.
edges.evidence: Controlled dose-escalation study in 15-18 anticoagulated volunteers; authors advise avoiding MK-7 supplements with VKAs

edges.mechanism: Starting, stopping or skipping the product changes INR in VKA-treated users; low-dose vitamin K (150 mcg) changes INR variability.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=70) and dose-response study; Cochrane review of 2 RCTs

edges.mechanism: Vitamin K (MK-4) lowers DCP, the HCC tumour marker, and PIVKA-II reflects vitamin K status; supplementation may mask DCP elevation.
edges.evidence: Small clinical pharmacology study in HCC/vitamin K deficiency; RCT data on PIVKA-II as vitamin K status marker

edges.mechanism: Vitamin K lowers dp-ucMGP and ucOC, so these status biomarkers reflect intake rather than disease change.
Duplicates phylloquinone (product already 1500 mcg); adds to vitamin K load relevant to VKA users.
edges.evidence: Inferred from ingredient overlap; K1 5 mg/d tolerated for 4 y in ECKO

edges.mechanism: Duplicates MK-7 (product already 600 mcg, near top of trial doses); long half-life increases accumulation and VKA interference.
edges.evidence: Inferred from overlap; dose-response VKA study; RCT doses 180-720 mcg/d

edges.mechanism: Duplicates MK-4 (product 5 mg); 45 mg/d MK-4 raised adverse events (RR 1.47) vs placebo in MA.
Duplicates lutein 10 mg/zeaxanthin 2 mg (15/3 mg on older softgel label); stacking can exceed the 20 mg/d lutein Observed Safe Level.
Duplicates lycopene 15 mg; Observed Safe Level 75 mg/d, so stacking mainly adds cost and carotenodermia risk.
edges.evidence: Risk assessment; small RCT of carotenodermia

edges.mechanism: Duplicates astaxanthin 12 mg, already above EFSA's 8 mg/day supplement level; stacking further raises exposure; astaxanthin had anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects in animals.
edges.evidence: EFSA opinion; safety review; preclinical data

edges.mechanism: High-dose vitamin E (1000 IU/d) increased PIVKA-II, i.e. antagonized vitamin K; may partly offset vitamin K effects and alter anticoagulant response.
edges.evidence: 2 RCTs (n=70) of vitamin E on vitamin K status

edges.mechanism: K2 was tested combined with D3 (25 mcg) in AVADEC and DANCODE; DANCODE slowed CAC progression, AVADEC did not slow valve calcification.
edges.evidence: RCTs; contribution of each vitamin not separable

edges.mechanism: Astaxanthin inhibited platelet activation comparably to aspirin in rodents; additive antiplatelet effect theoretical.
edges.evidence: Preclinical only; one human warfarin case report

edges.mechanism: Lipase inhibition reduces absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and carotenoids; label advises taking vitamins >=2 h apart.
2.5 g/d sterols/stanols lower plasma lycopene (-12.3%), zeaxanthin (-12.9%), lutein (-7.4%).
Product has no beta-carotene; lutein/zeaxanthin was not significantly associated with lung cancer (OR 1.15) whereas beta-carotene was (OR 1.82).
DCP/PIVKA-II tumour marker falls with vitamin K, potentially masking HCC signal.
EFSA found the astaxanthin ADI reached or exceeded in under-18s at 8 mg/day; product supplies 12 mg.
